title: The interview that wasn't
paragraphs: When Laura applied for a job at a small games company, she was {confident} that she would be asked the usual questions. Instead, the {interviewer} handed her a box of building blocks and asked her to make something in ten minutes. Laura was {completely} confused, but she decided to make the most of this {unexpected} challenge.

Ten minutes later she had built a small bridge, which she {proudly} presented to the panel. The company later explained that the test had nothing to do with {creativity}. What really interested them was how candidates behaved under {pressure}. Some people panicked, some complained that the task was {useless}, and a few simply walked out.

The team found Laura's calm response {impressive}, and she was offered the job the following day. Today, she is responsible for the {selection} of new staff herself and, {unsurprisingly}, she uses exactly the same test.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-ent)
gaps.explanation: CONFIDENCE → confident. Después de 'was' y antes de 'that' va un adjetivo.

gaps.label: Persona (-er)
gaps.explanation: INTERVIEW → interviewer. Quien 'handed her a box' es una persona: -er.

gaps.label: Adverbio (-ly)
gaps.explanation: COMPLETE → completely. Modifica al adjetivo 'confused': va un adverbio.

gaps.label: Prefijo negativo (un-) + -ed
gaps.explanation: EXPECT → unexpected. Delante de 'challenge' va un adjetivo, y el sentido es negativo: no se lo esperaba.

gaps.label: Adverbio (-ly)
gaps.explanation: PROUD → proudly. Describe CÓMO presentó el puente: adverbio.

gaps.label: Sustantivo (-ivity)
gaps.explanation: CREATE → creativity. Después de 'to do with' va un sustantivo.

gaps.label: Sustantivo (-ure)
gaps.explanation: PRESS → pressure. 'under pressure' = bajo presión.

gaps.label: Adjetivo negativo (-less)
gaps.explanation: USE → useless. 'complained' anuncia algo negativo: -LESS = sin.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-ive)
gaps.explanation: IMPRESS → impressive. 'found something + adjetivo'.

gaps.label: Sustantivo (-ion)
gaps.explanation: SELECT → selection. Después de 'the' y antes de 'of' va un sustantivo.

gaps.label: Prefijo negativo (un-) + adverbio
gaps.explanation: SURPRISE → unsurprisingly. Adverbio de oración, y negativo: era lo esperable que usara el mismo test.

title: Still running at seventy
paragraphs: Most people of seventy would find the idea of running a marathon {unbelievable}. But for Margaret Hill, who only took up running in her sixties, it has become a {yearly} tradition. The first time, her family watched {anxiously} as she crossed the finish line, but her doctor now admits that her {fitness} is better than that of many of his younger patients.

Margaret's {training} is simple: she runs five days a week, whatever the weather. She says the hardest part is not the running itself but learning to rest: she finds {relaxation} far more difficult than exercise. Without her running club, she adds, her life would feel {incomplete}.

Her {expectations} have changed over the years. She no longer worries about her time; she simply wants to finish {comfortably}. Last year she finished, {surprisingly}, ahead of runners half her age, and she talks {confidently} about running another ten marathons.

gaps.label: Prefijo negativo (un-) + -able
gaps.explanation: BELIEVE → unbelievable. 'find something + adjetivo', con sentido negativo.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-ly)
gaps.explanation: YEAR → yearly. Algunos adjetivos terminan en -LY: yearly, daily, friendly.

gaps.label: Adverbio (-ously)
gaps.explanation: ANXIETY → anxious → anxiously. Describe CÓMO miraba la familia.

gaps.label: Sustantivo (-ness)
gaps.explanation: FIT → fitness. Después de 'her' va un sustantivo. Ojo: no se duplica la T.

gaps.label: Sustantivo (-ation)
gaps.explanation: RELAX → relaxation. Es el objeto de 'finds': un sustantivo.

gaps.explanation: COMPLETE → incomplete. Sin el club, a su vida le faltaría algo. El negativo de COMPLETE es con IN-.

gaps.label: Sustantivo plural (-ation)
gaps.explanation: EXPECT → expectations. Va plural: 'have changed' concuerda con un sujeto plural.

gaps.explanation: SURPRISE → surprisingly. Adverbio de comentario entre comas: fue sorprendente.

gaps.label: Adverbio (-ently)
gaps.explanation: CONFIDENCE → confident → confidently. Describe CÓMO habla.

title: Dogs at the office
paragraphs: A growing number of companies now allow staff to bring their dogs to work, and the idea is becoming {increasingly} popular. Supporters claim that having animals around creates a more {relaxed} atmosphere. Owners also appreciate not having to pay for {expensive} dog-sitters, and many say they feel more {productive} when their pet is nearby.

However, not everyone is {enthusiastic}. Some workers suffer from {allergies}, while others are simply {frightened} of dogs. There are also {practical} problems: who is responsible if a dog damages the furniture?

Most companies have therefore introduced strict rules about pets' {behaviour}. Dogs that are noisy or {aggressive} are not allowed back, and owners are expected to be {respectful} of colleagues who do not like animals. Some managers even say that lunchtime dog walks have made their teams more {creative}.

gaps.label: Adverbio (-ingly)
gaps.explanation: INCREASE → increasingly. Modifica al adjetivo 'popular'.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-ed)
gaps.explanation: RELAX → relaxed. Delante de 'atmosphere' va un adjetivo. 'Relaxing' también existe, pero un ambiente 'relaxed' es el que se vive tranquilo.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-ive)
gaps.explanation: EXPENSE → expensive. Delante del sustantivo 'dog-sitters' va un adjetivo.

gaps.explanation: ALLERGIC → allergy → allergies. 'suffer from' + sustantivo; va en plural porque no hay artículo.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-ened)
gaps.explanation: FRIGHT → frightened. 'frightened of' = tenerle miedo a algo. Es como se SIENTE la persona: -ed.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-al)
gaps.explanation: PRACTICE → practical. Delante de 'problems' va un adjetivo.

gaps.label: Sustantivo (-iour)
gaps.explanation: BEHAVE → behaviour (británico) o behavior (americano). Después de 'pets'' va un sustantivo.

gaps.explanation: AGGRESSION → aggressive. Coordinado con 'noisy': otro adjetivo.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-ful)
gaps.explanation: RESPECT → respectful = respetuoso. 'Respected' sería 'respetado', y no encaja con 'of colleagues'.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-ive)
gaps.explanation: CREATE → creative. 'made their teams more + adjetivo'.

title: My year without a smartphone
paragraphs: Six months ago, I made a decision that my friends still find {extraordinary}: I gave up my smartphone and replaced it with a basic phone that can only make calls. The first week was deeply {uncomfortable}. I kept reaching for my pocket {automatically}, and I always felt {anxious} whenever I could not check the news.

Without maps, I got lost {regularly} and often had to stop strangers to ask for {directions}. Most of them, to my {astonishment}, were happy to help. I also rediscovered the {pleasure} of reading a book on the train, and I began to enjoy a sense of {freedom} that I had almost forgotten.
My {concentration} has improved enormously, and I sleep much better. Of course, there are {disadvantages}. Some of my friends find me {impossible} to contact, but I have no {intention} of going back.

gaps.explanation: ORDINARY → extraordinary. 'find something + adjetivo'; EXTRA- = fuera de lo común.

gaps.explanation: COMFORT → uncomfortable. Después de 'was deeply' va un adjetivo, y negativo.

gaps.explanation: AUTOMATIC → automatically. Los adjetivos en -IC forman el adverbio con -ALLY.

gaps.explanation: PLEASE → pleasure. Después de 'the' y antes de 'of' va un sustantivo.

gaps.explanation: FREE → freedom. 'a sense of + sustantivo'.

gaps.explanation: CONCENTRATE → concentration. Después de 'my' va un sustantivo.

gaps.explanation: ADVANTAGE → disadvantages. 'Of course' anuncia lo negativo, y 'there are' pide plural.

gaps.explanation: POSSIBLE → impossible. Delante de P, el negativo es IM-.

gaps.label: Sustantivo (-tion)
gaps.explanation: INTEND → intention. 'have no intention of + -ing' = no tener intención de.

title: The town that grows its own food
paragraphs: Ten years ago, a group of {residents} in a small English town started planting vegetables in public spaces. Their aim was to make the town less {dependent} on supermarkets. At first, many people thought the plan was completely {impractical}. Today, however, herbs and vegetables grow {freely} outside the police station, the school and even the railway station.

The project's {organisers} say that anyone can take what they need {directly} from the beds. There has been {remarkably} little theft or damage. Tourism has also {unexpectedly} increased, as visitors come from all over the world to see this {unusual} experiment.

Local schools regularly organise {educational} visits to the gardens, and several groups of gardening {enthusiasts} in other towns have copied the idea with equal {success}. The founders admit that feeding a whole town is still a distant dream, but they remain {optimistic} about the future.

gaps.label: Persona (-ent)
gaps.explanation: RESIDE → residents. 'a group of' + personas, en plural.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-ent)

gaps.explanation: PRACTICE → impractical. 'At first' y 'however' anuncian que al principio lo veían negativo.

gaps.explanation: EXPECT → unexpectedly. Entre 'has' e 'increased' va un adverbio, y nadie lo esperaba.

gaps.label: Prefijo negativo (un-)
gaps.explanation: USUAL → unusual. Vienen de todo el mundo porque es algo raro.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-al)
gaps.explanation: EDUCATE → education → educational. Delante de 'visits' va un adjetivo.

gaps.label: Persona (-ast)
gaps.explanation: ENTHUSIASM → enthusiasts. 'groups of gardening ___' son personas, en plural.

gaps.label: Sustantivo
gaps.explanation: SUCCEED → success. 'with equal + sustantivo'.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-istic)
gaps.explanation: OPTIMISM → optimistic. 'remain + adjetivo'.

title: From gamer to surgeon
paragraphs: As a teenager, Daniel spent so many hours playing video games that his parents were {seriously} worried. His teachers described him as {intelligent} but lazy, and few people expected him to be {successful}. Today, at thirty-four, he is one of the country's most {respected} surgeons.

Daniel believes that his {childhood} hobby was actually an important part of his {education}. Research seems to support him: one study found that surgeons who play video games work more {accurately} than those who do not. The {ability} to coordinate hand and eye is essential in modern surgery, where many {operations} are carried out using cameras and remote controls, and some hospitals are now considering the {possibility} of using games in training.

Daniel is careful not to give the {impression} that games are a shortcut to medicine. 'I still had to study {incredibly} hard,' he says, with obvious {pride}. But he does think parents should be less {critical} of their children's hobbies. 'You never know which skills will turn out to be {useful}.'

gaps.explanation: SERIOUS → seriously. Modifica al adjetivo 'worried'.

gaps.explanation: ABLE → ability. 'The ability to' + infinitivo = la capacidad de.

gaps.label: Sustantivo plural (-ion)
gaps.explanation: OPERATE → operations. 'many' pide plural.

gaps.label: Sustantivo (-ility)
gaps.explanation: POSSIBLE → possibility. 'the ___ of + -ing' pide un sustantivo.

gaps.label: Sustantivo (-ion)
gaps.explanation: IMPRESS → impression. 'give the impression that' = dar la impresión de que.

gaps.label: Prefijo negativo (in-) + adverbio
gaps.explanation: CREDIBLE → incredibly. Intensifica a 'hard'; el prefijo IN- le da el sentido de 'increíblemente'.

gaps.label: Sustantivo (irregular)
gaps.explanation: PROUD → pride. 'with obvious + sustantivo'. Es irregular: no se dice 'proudness'.

gaps.explanation: CRITIC → critical. 'less critical of' = menos crítico con.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-ful)
gaps.explanation: USE → useful. 'turn out to be + adjetivo', con sentido positivo.

title: Dinner for twelve
paragraphs: When my flatmate announced that he was going to cook dinner for twelve people, I was {surprised}: he had never made anything more {ambitious} than toast. Still, he had just finished a short course with a {professional} chef, and he was {unusually} calm about the whole thing.

The first hour went {smoothly}, and everything seemed fine. Then, {unfortunately}, the oven stopped working, and soon the smoke alarm was making a {frightening} noise. Most of our guests, {luckily}, found the whole situation very funny.

In the end we ordered pizza, and the evening turned out to be a {memorable} one. My flatmate has not given up, though. He says the experience taught him the {importance} of preparation, and next time he plans to use a more {reliable} oven.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-ed)
gaps.explanation: SURPRISE → surprised. Es cómo me SENTÍ yo: adjetivo en -ED.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-ious)

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-al)
gaps.explanation: PROFESSION → professional. Delante de 'chef' va un adjetivo.

gaps.label: Prefijo negativo (un-) + adverbio
gaps.explanation: USUAL → unusually. Modifica a 'calm', y el sentido es 'más de lo normal'.

gaps.explanation: SMOOTH → smoothly. 'go smoothly' = salir bien, sin problemas.

gaps.label: Prefijo negativo (un-) + adverbio

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-ening)

gaps.label: Adverbio (-ily)
gaps.explanation: LUCK → lucky → luckily. Adverbio de comentario entre comas.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-able)
gaps.explanation: MEMORY → memorable = que se recuerda. 'a ___ one' pide un adjetivo.

gaps.label: Sustantivo (-ance)
gaps.explanation: IMPORTANT → importance. Después de 'the' y antes de 'of' va un sustantivo.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-iable)
gaps.explanation: RELY → reliable = confiable. 'a more + adjetivo + oven'.

title: Goodbye, city
paragraphs: Three years ago, my partner and I made the {decision} to leave our flat in the city in search of {simplicity}. Our friends thought the plan was completely {unrealistic}, and to be honest, the first winter was {unbelievably} hard.

The nearest shop was a twenty-minute drive away, and the internet was so {unreliable} that working from home required a lot of {patience}. Slowly, though, we adapted. We learnt to plan our shopping {carefully}, and our neighbours turned out to be extremely {helpful}.

Today, I can't imagine living anywhere else. My stress levels have dropped {considerably}, and I sleep more {peacefully} than I have in years. Country life is not for everyone, but for us it has been a {wonderful} experience.

gaps.explanation: DECIDE → decision. 'make a decision' = tomar una decisión.

gaps.label: Sustantivo (-icity)

gaps.explanation: REAL → realistic → unrealistic. Los amigos creían que el plan no iba a funcionar: negativo.

gaps.explanation: BELIEVE → unbelievably. Intensifica a 'hard': increíblemente difícil.

gaps.explanation: RELY → unreliable. Un internet que falla no es confiable: negativo.

gaps.label: Adverbio (-fully)

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-ful)
gaps.explanation: WONDER → wonderful. Delante de 'experience' va un adjetivo.

title: A robot in the classroom
paragraphs: When a primary school in Yorkshire introduced a robot teaching {assistant}, many parents reacted with {suspicion}. They worried that the machine would make human teachers {unnecessary}, or that children would develop an unhealthy {dependence} on technology.

A year later, the results are {encouraging}. The robot takes care of {repetitive} tasks such as checking spelling, which allows teachers to plan their lessons more {creatively}. Shy children, in particular, seem {comfortable} asking the robot questions they would be too {embarrassed} to ask in front of the class.

Not everyone is convinced. Critics point out that the robot cost the school a {considerable} amount of money, and that it is still {unable} to cope with the {unpredictable} situations that arise in every classroom.

gaps.explanation: ASSIST → assistant. 'a robot teaching ___' es quien ayuda: persona (-ANT).

gaps.label: Prefijo negativo (un-) + -able
gaps.explanation: PREDICT → unpredictable. Lo que pasa en un aula no se puede prever.

title: The joy of getting lost
paragraphs: On my last holiday, I tried something completely {different}: I left my phone at the hotel and explored the city {entirely} on foot, without a map. At first I felt quite {nervous}, but that feeling soon turned into a wonderful sense of {excitement}.

Without a screen to look at, I noticed details I would {usually} miss. Everywhere I looked there were {colourful} doors, tiny cafés and hidden gardens. I also had to depend on the {kindness} of strangers. Once, I got {hopelessly} lost, and an old man walked me all the way back to my hotel.
Travelling like this is not always {convenient}, and I did waste a lot of time. But it was the most {relaxing} holiday I have ever had, and I {strongly} recommend trying it at least once.

gaps.label: Adverbio (-ly)
gaps.explanation: STRONG → strongly. 'strongly recommend' = recomendar mucho.

title: The power of no
paragraphs: For many people, turning down a request feels rude or even {unkind}. We worry that the other person will see us as {unhelpful}, so we agree to things we do not {necessarily} want to do.

The problem is that saying yes to everything is simply not {realistic}. Sooner or later, we become tired and {impatient} with the people we love. Psychologists suggest refusing {politely} but firmly, and without feeling the need to give a long {explanation}.

At first, this may cause some {discomfort}, but most people react far more {positively} than we expect. And with practice, we become more {decisive}. After all, every time you say no to something {unimportant}, you are saying yes to something that really matters.

gaps.label: Prefijo negativo (un-)
gaps.explanation: KIND → unkind = poco amable. Va con 'rude': otro adjetivo negativo.

gaps.label: Prefijo negativo (un-) + -ful

gaps.label: Adverbio (-ily)

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-istic)
gaps.explanation: REAL → realistic. El 'not' ya está en la frase: el adjetivo va en positivo.

gaps.label: Prefijo negativo (im-)
gaps.explanation: PATIENT → impatient. Delante de P, el negativo es IM-. Va con 'tired'.

gaps.label: Adverbio (-ly)

gaps.label: Sustantivo (-ation)

gaps.label: Prefijo negativo (dis-)
gaps.explanation: COMFORT → discomfort = incomodidad. 'some + sustantivo', con sentido negativo.

gaps.label: Adverbio (-ly)
gaps.explanation: POSITIVE → positively. 'react far more + adverbio'.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-sive)
gaps.explanation: DECIDE → decisive = decidido, firme. 'become more + adjetivo'.

gaps.label: Prefijo negativo (un-)
gaps.explanation: IMPORTANT → unimportant. Contrasta con 'something that really matters'.

title: A museum of mistakes
paragraphs: There is a small museum in the north of England with a rather {surprising} collection. Instead of masterpieces, it displays products that were completely {unsuccessful}: drinks nobody wanted, gadgets nobody could use and toys that turned out to be {dangerous}.

The museum's {creator}, a former business consultant, says his aim is not to laugh at these products. 'Every {failure} teaches us something,' he explains. 'Companies prefer to hide their most {embarrassing} mistakes, so nobody learns from them.' In his view, many of these failures were {predictable} from the start.

Many {visitors} say they find the whole exhibition {strangely} comforting. Seeing that even huge companies make {disastrous} decisions makes their own mistakes seem more {forgivable}. Perhaps that is the museum's most {valuable} lesson.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-ing)
gaps.explanation: SURPRISE → surprising. La colección CAUSA sorpresa: -ING.

gaps.label: Prefijo negativo (un-) + -ful
gaps.explanation: SUCCEED → successful → unsuccessful. Son productos que fracasaron.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-ous)
gaps.explanation: DANGER → dangerous. 'turned out to be + adjetivo'.

gaps.label: Persona (-or)
gaps.explanation: CREATE → creator. Es una persona: 'a former business consultant'.

gaps.label: Sustantivo (-ure)
gaps.explanation: FAIL → failure. 'Every + sustantivo singular'.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-ing)
gaps.explanation: EMBARRASS → embarrassing. Los errores CAUSAN vergüenza: -ING.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-able)
gaps.explanation: PREDICT → predictable = previsible. 'from the start' indica que se podía ver venir.

gaps.label: Persona plural (-or)
gaps.explanation: VISIT → visitors. 'Many' pide plural.

gaps.label: Adverbio (-ly)
gaps.explanation: STRANGE → strangely. Modifica al adjetivo 'comforting'.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-rous)
gaps.explanation: DISASTER → disastrous. Ojo: se cae la E (disaster → disastr-ous).

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-able)
gaps.explanation: FORGIVE → forgivable = perdonable. 'seem more + adjetivo'. Se cae la E final.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-able)
gaps.explanation: VALUE → valuable. 'the museum's most + adjetivo + lesson'.

title: A festival of flavours
paragraphs: Every summer, our town holds a street food festival, and this year's was the most {exciting} yet. More than fifty stalls offered food from a huge {variety} of countries, and the streets were full of {cheerful} music.

My favourite stall was run by a Korean family whose dumplings were {absolutely} delicious. I arrived early, {fortunately}, because by midday they had sold out. Other people were {unlucky} and missed them completely. There was also a {competition} for the best dessert, which was won by a ten-year-old girl and her {wonderfully} simple apple cake.
The festival is free to enter, and the atmosphere is always {friendly}. If you live nearby, I would {definitely} recommend a visit, but make sure you arrive {hungry}!

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-ing)
gaps.explanation: EXCITE → exciting. El festival CAUSA emoción: -ING.

gaps.label: Sustantivo (-iety)
gaps.explanation: VARY → variety. 'a huge + sustantivo + of'.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-ful)
gaps.explanation: CHEER → cheerful = alegre. Delante de 'music' va un adjetivo.

gaps.label: Adverbio (-ly)
gaps.explanation: ABSOLUTE → absolutely. Intensifica a 'delicious'.

gaps.label: Adverbio (-ly)
gaps.explanation: FORTUNATE → fortunately. Adverbio de comentario: por suerte llegué temprano.

gaps.label: Prefijo negativo (un-) + -y
gaps.explanation: LUCK → lucky → unlucky. Se perdieron los dumplings: negativo.

gaps.label: Sustantivo (-ition)
gaps.explanation: COMPETE → competition. 'a + sustantivo + for'.

gaps.label: Adverbio (-fully)
gaps.explanation: WONDER → wonderful → wonderfully. Modifica al adjetivo 'simple'.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-ly)
gaps.explanation: FRIEND → friendly. Es un ADJETIVO aunque termine en -LY.

gaps.label: Adverbio (-ly)
gaps.explanation: DEFINITE → definitely. Ojo con la ortografía: defin-I-tely.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-y)
gaps.explanation: HUNGER → hungry. 'arrive + adjetivo' = llegar con hambre.

title: A box of recipes
paragraphs: When my grandmother died, she left me a box of recipes, each one written in her {beautiful} handwriting. Many of them were {practically} impossible to follow. She never used exact {measurements}, and her instructions were often {frustratingly} vague: 'a little butter' or 'cook until ready'.

Still, I was {determined} to cook every dish at least once. My first attempt at her fish soup was completely {inedible}, but I kept trying {patiently}. Over the following months, the dishes {gradually} began to taste the way I remembered.
Cooking her recipes has become a {comforting} ritual, and my children now have their own {favourites}. In a way, she is still feeding her family, which I find {deeply} moving.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-iful)
gaps.explanation: BEAUTY → beautiful. La Y pasa a I: beaut-i-ful.

gaps.label: Adverbio (-ally)
gaps.explanation: PRACTICE → practical → practically = prácticamente, casi.

gaps.label: Sustantivo plural (-ment)
gaps.explanation: MEASURE → measurements. 'exact + sustantivo', en plural.

gaps.label: Adverbio (-ingly)
gaps.explanation: FRUSTRATE → frustrating → frustratingly. Modifica a 'vague'.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-ed)
gaps.explanation: DETERMINATION → determined. 'be determined to' = estar decidido a.

gaps.label: Prefijo negativo (in-)
gaps.explanation: EDIBLE → inedible = incomible. El 'but I kept trying' anuncia que salió mal.

gaps.label: Adverbio (-ently)
gaps.explanation: PATIENT → patiently. Describe CÓMO seguí intentando.

gaps.label: Adverbio (-ly)
gaps.explanation: GRADUAL → gradually = poco a poco.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-ing)
gaps.explanation: COMFORT → comforting = reconfortante. El ritual CAUSA consuelo: -ING.

gaps.label: Sustantivo plural (-ite)
gaps.explanation: FAVOUR → favourites (británico) o favorites (americano). 'their own + sustantivo plural'.

gaps.label: Adverbio (-ly)
gaps.explanation: DEEP → deeply. Modifica al adjetivo 'moving'.

title: The café is my office
paragraphs: Walk into any café in the city centre and you will find people working {silently} on their laptops. For many {employees}, working from a café has become a {pleasant} alternative to the office. Some say the background noise helps them work more {efficiently}, while others simply enjoy feeling less {isolated}.
Café owners have {understandably} mixed feelings. Customers who stay for five hours after buying a single coffee are not exactly {profitable}, and some cafés have made their wifi {deliberately} slow.

Most remote workers, however, are {perfectly} happy to buy something every hour or so, and many say they feel a {responsibility} to support local businesses. After all, in such a {competitive} market, a café full of loyal customers is never a bad thing.

gaps.label: Adverbio (-ly)
gaps.explanation: SILENT → silently. Describe CÓMO trabajan.

gaps.label: Persona plural (-ee)
gaps.explanation: EMPLOY → employees = empleados. -EE es quien RECIBE la acción; -ER (employer) es quien emplea.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-ant)
gaps.explanation: PLEASE → pleasant = agradable. Delante de 'alternative' va un adjetivo.

gaps.label: Adverbio (-ly)
gaps.explanation: EFFICIENT → efficiently. 'work more + adverbio'.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-ed)
gaps.explanation: ISOLATE → isolated = aislado. 'feel less + adjetivo'.

gaps.label: Adverbio (-ably)
gaps.explanation: UNDERSTAND → understandable → understandably = comprensiblemente.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-able)
gaps.explanation: PROFIT → profitable = rentable. 'not exactly + adjetivo'.

gaps.label: Adverbio (-ly)
gaps.explanation: DELIBERATE → deliberately = a propósito. Modifica a 'slow'.

gaps.label: Adverbio (-ly)
gaps.explanation: PERFECT → perfectly. 'perfectly happy' = totalmente dispuestos.

gaps.label: Sustantivo (-ibility)
gaps.explanation: RESPONSIBLE → responsibility. 'feel a + sustantivo + to'.

gaps.label: Adjetivo (-itive)
gaps.explanation: COMPETE → competitive. Delante de 'market' va un adjetivo.
